title: no-skipped-tests/no-disabled-tests miss Playwright's test.describe.skip()
reproducingTestCommand: pnpm --filter @harness-engineering/eslint-plugin exec vitest run tests/rules/no-skipped-tests.test.ts tests/rules/no-disabled-tests.test.ts

reproducingTestResult.beforeFix: FAIL — 6 failed | 37 passed (43); AssertionError: Should have 1 error but had 0
reproducingTestResult.revertVerification: fix reverted with tests unchanged -> 6 failed | 37 passed; fix restored -> 43 passed

rootCause: Both rules gated skip detection on `node.callee.object.type === 'Identifier'`, which admits only a single-level member expression. Playwright namespaces its API, so `test.describe.skip()` has a MemberExpression (`test.describe`) as the callee object and never matched.
fix: Added `isTestModifierCall` to packages/eslint-plugin/src/utils/ast-helpers.ts, which resolves the callee to its dotted chain and matches any chain rooted at describe/it/test whose final link is the given modifier. Both rules now delegate to it for the `skip` modifier.
assumptions: Rule contract is NOT expanded beyond the `skip` keyword. The issue and the sibling rule `no-focused-tests` also mention `.only`/`.fixme`, but neither no-skipped-tests nor no-disabled-tests ever claimed those keywords, so they are left alone. The new helper is parameterised by modifier so a future change can adopt it without another rewrite.

The chain root must still be one of `describe` / `it` / `test`. A `.skip` on any other receiver (e.g. `rateLimiter.skip()`) stays unreported — pinned by new valid test cases so it cannot regress into a false positive.

Only statically written, non-computed dotted paths are matched. Computed access (`test.describe['skip']()`) and optional chaining (`test?.describe?.skip()`) resolve to null and stay unreported. This gap is pre-existing and identical in the flat case (`describe['skip']()` was never caught either); it has a different root cause from #1812 and was deliberately left out of scope rather than folded in silently.

`no-focused-tests` carries the identical flat-member guard for `.only`, so `test.describe.only()` is very likely missed the same way. Out of scope for #1812 (different rule, different keyword) and NOT fixed here; noted for follow-up.

Both rules keep firing independently on the same node, so a single `test.describe.skip` now reports twice when both rules are enabled — matching the pre-existing double-report behaviour for `test.skip` shown in the issue. Deduplicating the two overlapping rules is a separate design question, not a bug fix.
outOfScope: Rule message wording — the issue's 'Also worth considering' note asks the message to acknowledge a sanctioned quarantine as a third option alongside re-enable/delete. That is a copy/policy change, not the reported defect, and is not made here.
debugSessionNote: The harness-debugging pipeline writes its session to .harness/debug/resolved/1812-playwright-describe-skip.md, which is gitignored (.harness/.gitignore line 4). A verbatim copy is committed here so the investigation record is durable and reviewable.
